Definition: properly, drought, i.e. (by implication) a desolation
BiblicalUsage: Chorbah is a waste place, a desolation, and the prophets use it for Jerusalem's ruin and its repair. Daniel reads that seventy years are accomplished in the desolations of Jerusalem, Ezekiel says God will make the land waste and a reproach, Ezra prays over the desolations God has begun to repair, and Isaiah sees lambs feeding in the waste places of the fat ones.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the waste places in these verses are both judgment and hope, because the same God who desolates also repairs. I hold that the lambs feeding in the waste are the picture of life returning where judgment fell.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile; Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
